description: Automatically name Herdr tabs and panes from your current work: Git branch, running process, and Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, Hermes and Antigravity sessions. No LLM, no external service.

## [0.24.0](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/compare/v0.23.1...v0.24.0) (2026-11-22)


### Features

* **desktop:** name unplaced core tabs ([2841729](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/commit/2841729af976e479644c6570c4ca858f9ae660b3))
* **desktop:** read and rename tabs in the core's layout document ([6b1d6bc](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/commit/6b1d6bc8fa722ef49c62d215c77b081c6664e7f3))


### Bug Fixes

* **resolver:** compare pi's directory frame without case ([1f698ac](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/commit/1f698ac40a1e82cd7905593de261bd97617b341b))

### Refactoring

* **app:** read the label options in a function of their own ([9c12cc2](https://github.com/kryptamine/herdr-auto-title/commit/9c12cc2dba95b052f89883d0e83271c2b7fe2a46))

detail.readme: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46fa98e7-416f-4cca-b024-82bc641cd0d2 A [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) plugin that names your tabs and panes from what they are doing: the Git branch, the running process, or the topic of a Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Grok, Hermes or Antigravity session. No LLM, no external service, and a tab you rename yourself stays yours. ## Install You need Herdr 0.8.2+ on macOS, Linux or Windows. ```sh herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title --ref stable herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart ``` `stable` is the latest release. On amd64 and arm64 the install downloads its binary; elsewhere it builds from source with Go 1.24+. On Windows the download needs Git for Windows' Bash, and Go without it. The second line starts the plugin now rather than at Herdr's next start. To update, keeping your configuration: ```sh herdr plugin update herdr.auto-title herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart ``` Herdr before 0.9.4 has no `plugin update`; rerun the install lines instead. An update stays on the ref you installed: a tag never moves, and no `--ref` follows `main`. To switch, install once with `--ref stable`. To run the latest commit on `main`, which can be ahead of the latest release, leave `--ref` out. Herdr then builds from source with Go 1.24+: ```sh herdr plugin install kryptamine/herdr-auto-title herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart ``` ## Herdr desktop app The [desktop app](https://herdr.dev/) has no plugins, so Auto Title runs there as a service of its own, started at every login on macOS, Linux and Windows. The mod installs it on all three platforms; Windows needs no Git Bash or Go. **With the mod:** ask the app's agent to add the mod in this repository's [`mod/`](mod/) folder, or copy `mod/mods/auto-title` into `~/.config/herdr-app/mods/` and merge [`mod/keys.json`](mod/keys.json) into `~/.config/herdr-app/keys.json` yourself. `cmd-alt-t` opens a popup; press `Install`. In a tab of its own it downloads the binary of the release the mod belongs to, checks it against `SHA256SUMS` and has it install itself. The same popup starts and updates it. Once a day the service asks GitHub whether a newer release is out, and opens the popup by itself once for each one. To remove Auto Title, have the service's copy uninstall itself: ```sh # macOS ~/Library/Application\ Support/herdr-auto-title/bin/herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall # Linux "${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/herdr-auto-title/herdr-auto-title" desktop uninstall ``` **By hand:** with a release binary, or one built with `make build`: ```sh ./herdr-auto-title desktop install # start now and at every login ./herdr-auto-title desktop uninstall # stop it and remove it ``` On Windows the popup prefers Git Bash and uses Windows PowerShell 5.1 when Git Bash is unavailable. If policy blocks PowerShell scripts, install Git for Windows or use a release binary directly. No Go installation is needed. On Windows the binary is `herdr-auto-title.exe`, and the service is a Task Scheduler task; its copy is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\herdr-auto-title\bin\herdr-auto-title.exe`, which `desktop uninstall` removes too. Installing again is the update. The service runs its own copy of the binary, so the one you ran can be deleted. Its log is `~/Library/Logs/herdr-auto-title.log` on macOS and `journalctl --user -u herdr-auto-title` on Linux. On Windows it keeps no log; run `herdr-auto-title.exe desktop` in a terminal to see one. **On a machine with no window:** when the app connects to herdr-core on another machine over SSH, the agents and their sessions run on that machine. Install Auto Title there with `desktop install`, and set `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_CORE_LAYOUT=true` and `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT=true` in its `config.env`. It then names tabs from those sessions using the core's layout document or, for tabs Ovis starts outside the document, terminal labels. What differs from Herdr TUI: - Only tabs are named: the desktop app has no pane labels or workspace topics. - Connected machines' tabs are named too, from their terminal titles, processes and directories. With Python 3.9 or newer on the machine, its Git branches are read as well, and on Linux the Codex session a terminal's own process holds. No remote Auto Title installation is needed. - The service does not see your shell's environment, so settings go in [`config.env`](#configuration), never in a shell profile. - `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` needs a Nerd Font as the app's `ui_font` in its `settings.json`, since the tab bar is drawn in that font. ## Recommended setup Three settings make Auto Title work as intended. Each is optional. **Create tabs without a name prompt.** Herdr asks for a name before it creates a tab, and a name typed there counts as your own, so Auto Title never names that tab. In Herdr's `config.toml`: ```toml [ui] prompt_new_tab_name = false ``` **Install Herdr's integration for each agent you use.** It tells Auto Title which session a pane holds, so the tab is named after that session. Without it, a tab says only what the agent puts in its terminal title, and for Antigravity CLI that is nothing but `agy`. ```sh herdr integration install claude # Claude Code herdr integration install codex # Codex herdr integration install antigravity-cli # Antigravity CLI herdr integration install grok # Grok Build herdr integration install hermes # Hermes Agent herdr integration install pi # Pi ``` **Show the topic in the sidebar.** Auto Title reports what each workspace's active tab is doing as `$topic`, and Herdr draws it only where a sidebar row asks for it. This keeps the name and branch on top, with the topic in bold under them: ```toml [ui.sidebar.spaces] rows = [ ["state_icon", "workspace", "branch", "git_status"], [{ token = "$topic", bold = true, dim = false }], ] ``` Each client reads its own `config.toml`, so set the rows on every machine you attach from. ## What you get ``` ~/work/dashboard → 1 · dashboard ~/work/dashboard on feature/MC-13200 → 2 · dashboard › MC-13200 nvim editing auth.provider.ts → 3 · nvim › auth.provider.ts an agent working on OAuth scopes → 4 · dashboard › Implement OAuth scopes ssh into prod-01 → 5 · ssh › prod-01 mosh into devbox → 6 · mosh › devbox $HOME → 7 · Shell ``` - The number in front is the tab's position, which is also the key that switches to it. - The default branch is left out. Other branches are cut down to what identifies them: `bugfix-asa-cpanel-uapi-mc-13675` becomes `MC-13675`. - A tab with several panes is named after the pane focused in it, whether the tab is shown or not. `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT=true` names it after its agent pane instead. - Each pane gets a name of its own, so Herdr's goto panel (`prefix`+`g`) no longer lists every Claude Code pane as `claude`. - Rename a tab or a pane yourself and Auto Title stops touching it. Clear the name to hand it back. - On Windows, Herdr reports only the shell or an agent running in a pane, so an editor or an ssh or mosh session does not name its tab. > [!WARNING] > In the default mode, the first start renames every pane, including panes you > had already named by hand. A pane you rename after that is left alone. > Session-only mode also protects existing names at startup. ## Configuration Every setting is optional. Copy [`config.env.example`](config.env.example) to `~/.config/herdr-auto-title/config.env` and uncomment what you need. That path works on every platform: on Windows it is under `%USERPROFILE%\.config`. Then [restart](#restarting): the file is read once at startup. Two other directories are read, and the first that already holds the file wins: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, when it is set to an absolute path, comes before `~/.config`, and `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS or `%APPDATA%` on Windows comes after it. The config directory that `herdr plugin list` prints is not read. | Setting | Default | What it does | | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DEBUG` | `false` | Log at DEBUG instead of INFO | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POLL_MS` | `500` | How often the session is read, in milliseconds | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH` | `50` | Longest title, in columns | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_BRANCH_MAX` | `12` | Longest branch in a title, in columns; `0` hides branches | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_DIRECTORY_MAX` | none | Longest directory in a tab title, in columns; `0` hides it, from pane labels too, wherever something else names them | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_POSITION` | `true` | Put the tab's position in front of its title | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE` | `manual-names.json`, found the same way | Where names you set by hand are kept; empty keeps them in memory | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT` | `true` | Read an agent's own session files: what it is doing, and where | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY` | `false` | Mirror session names only; keep labels when no usable name is ready | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_NAME` | `false` | Put the agent's name in front of what it is doing | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANES` | `true` | Name panes as well as tabs | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PREFER_AGENT` | `false` | Name a tab after its agent pane even while another pane is focused | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_CORE_LAYOUT` | `false` | Desktop mode: read and rename tabs through herdr-core without an app window | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_PANE_ID` | `false` | Put the pane's Herdr ID in front of its label, as `[w1:p2] api` | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_HANDLE` | `false` | Put the name `herdr agent rename` gave the pane's agent in front of its label, as `driver › api` | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_ICONS` | `false` | Put a Nerd Font 3.0+ icon for what a pane runs in front of labels | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_AGENT_STATUS` | `false` | Put the tab's agent status in front of its title: `◉` idle, `◐` working, `●` blocked, `✓` done | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACES` | `true` | Report what each workspace's active tab is doing as its `topic` | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_WORKSPACE_MAX_LENGTH` | none: Herdr fits it | Longest topic, in columns | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_CLAUDE_DIRS` | none | Extra Claude config homes to search, `:`-separated | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES` | none | Extra absolute Hermes homes to search, `:`-separated (`;` on Windows), including each home's named profiles | | `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_FOREIGN_PROCESSES` | none | Programs that own their tab and pane labels, so Auto Title leaves them alone; herdr-mirror's streamer is built in. `:`-separated | On Windows Herdr reports only the shell or a recognised agent per pane, so this setting and the built-in herdr-mirror check may not detect a label-owning program there. `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_TRANSCRIPT=false` also stops Hermes reads and drops the branch from a tab whose agent works in a git worktree: the transcript is what names that worktree. ### Session-only mode `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_SESSION_ONLY=true` names tabs and panes only from the name their agent session holds: Claude Code's title, Codex's index name, Pi's session name, Hermes's native title, Antigravity's annotation, Grok Build's generated title. - Until a usable name exists, the label stays as it is. No terminal title, process, directory or opening prompt stands in, even after `/new` or exit. - Names already set by hand are protected from the first poll. Turning the mode off keeps them locked; clear a name to hand it back. - Only Hermes says where its title came from, so another agent's stored name may still be prompt text. - Auto Title records the labels it set in `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_MANUAL_FILE`, so a restart does not mistake them for yours. That file therefore holds generated names too; left empty, nothing survives a restart. Details are in [title resolution](docs/architecture/title-resolution.md#session-only-mode). ### Hermes Hermes titles are read from `sessions.title` in its `state.db`, read-only: no chat messages, no LLM call. They need a Herdr integration that reports the Hermes session ID. Auto Title looks in the foreground process's `HERMES_HOME` on Linux, then in the plugin's `HERMES_HOME`, `HERDR_AUTO_TITLE_HERMES_HOMES` and `~/.hermes`, each with its `profiles/*`. Paths must be absolute. A session found in two homes names nothing. Details are in [Hermes session titles](docs/architecture/hermes-session-titles.md). ## Restarting ```sh herdr plugin action invoke herdr.auto-title.restart ``` This starts a fresh Auto Title in place of the running one, and a notification says how it went. Run it after an update, after changing the configuration, or when the plugin has stopped naming tabs. On Windows the action needs Herdr 0.9.0 or newer. An upgrade from a version before 0.8.0 needs one `herdr server stop` instead: that instance does not know to leave. ## Documentation - [Architecture](docs/architecture/): how the plugin works and why. - [Development](docs/development.md): working on the plugin. ## Contributors
